column1: # Reviewed privileged-event jobs allowed on persistent runners (ADR 0235).
# The digest covers the job, its inherited workflow trigger/env/permissions/
# defaults, every calling job, the scanned-tree bytes the job puts on disk
# (exact non-cone sparse paths, cone-mode directories with root and parent
# files, local action directories), and its unresolved reasons. Any edit turns
# the entry STALE. The checker over-approximates: a fetch, a runtime tree
# change, a non-default shell, a full or runtime-selected checkout, submodules,
# or head detection that materializes or cannot decide leaves the job
# unresolved, and dynamic: must name exactly the reason categories the checker
# prints, with a justification specific to what this job fetches or changes.

column4: Runs only for merged PRs (trigger types: [closed], if: merged); sparse-checks out scripts/ci-gate/post-merge-reconcile.sh at github.sha (the base-branch commit this workflow file is read from, so the reviewed bytes) with persist-credentials false and executes only that script (its bytes are in this digest) plus inline gh/jq; head SHA/ref/repo are API identifiers; the merge-attestation-<run> artifact must come from a successful default-branch workflow_dispatch run from the canonical ai-review-merge-dispatch.yml wrapper or the exact ai-review-merge.yml adopter/legacy path and attestation.json is schema-validated with jq as data
column5: dynamic: fetch: every gh api call (step 2 and post-merge-reconcile.sh) returns JSON that only jq parses, plus one gh api download of the merge-attestation-<run> zip from the exact current or legacy dispatcher run that the check-run, review, and dispatch-job queries just validated; unzip -p extracts only attestation.json into a 0700 RUNNER_TEMP directory, jq schema-validates it, and the script reads it as data to file issues and delete the merged head ref; nothing fetched is executed or written into the checkout

column4: Same job as the gate-rearm.yml [pull_request_target] entry, reached standalone through an adopter's workflow_call: No checkout or source-fetching action; executes only inline bash and heredoc-authored Python from the base workflow plus gh/jq API calls; PR head SHA and number are compared as data; ai-review-arm-<run>-<attempt> receipts come from trusted gate-rearm runs whose workflow blob is matched to the default branch, are downloaded to a mktemp directory, and are read only as data with jq; caller workflow blobs fetched through the git/blobs API are hashed, never executed; canonical direct dispatch is fixed to ai-review-merge-dispatch.yml and adopter dispatch stays ai-review-merge.yml
column5: dynamic: fetch: the job has no checkout; gh api responses (check runs, runs, artifacts, PR files, git trees and blobs) are JSON parsed by jq or by json.loads in the heredoc-authored bootstrap classifier, and fetched workflow blobs are hashed and compared, never executed; gh run download extracts ai-review-arm receipts into fresh mktemp RUNNER_TEMP directories that are read only with jq and removed; the urllib match is urllib.parse.quote, URL encoding with no network access

column4: Owner-dispatched fleet canary on an exact self-hosted runner label: no checkout of repository source; inline Dockerfile and pinned service/tool images only; GITHUB_SHA and inputs are recorded as receipt metadata via jq; gh api reads the canary job id as JSON data; upload-artifact publishes only the generated receipt JSON. Persistent placement is required to prove the named runner. DOWNLOAD no longer treats curlimages/curl image refs as head-materializing curl invocations (Part of #1831).
column5: dynamic: fetch: curl appears only as the pinned curlimages/curl image reference inside `docker run` (not a host curl invocation); docker build/create/run use heredoc Dockerfile and digest-pinned images with no repository checkout; gh api returns JSON that only jq parses for the job id; services.postgres pulls the digest-pinned postgres image at job start and is used only for pg_isready health — nothing fetched is executed as repository head content
